findings.title: SQL injection in product catalog category filter
findings.evidence: User-controlled query parameter category is interpolated into SQL via f-string: statement = f"SELECT id, title, published FROM products WHERE category = '{category}' AND published = 1", then executed with self.db.execute(statement). Violates the documented contract that the catalog returns only published products in the requested category.
findings.attack_path: Unauthenticated client → GET /api/products?category=... → parse_qs yields category → string-built SELECT → sqlite3 execute → unpublished or out-of-category rows returned (e.g. Unannounced draft).

validation.result: In-memory create_app().dispatch('/api/products', "category=books' OR published=0 OR category='", '') returned HTTP 200 including product id 2 title 'Unannounced draft' with published=0; normal category=books returned only the published books row.

findings.title: Missing invoice ownership authorization (IDOR)
findings.evidence: After mapping Authorization to user, invoice_id is loaded with a parameterized SELECT by id only; row is returned without comparing row owner to the authenticated user. Documented contract: a signed-in user can read only their own invoices.
findings.attack_path: Authenticated low-privilege user (Bearer alice-test-token) → GET /api/invoices/2 → auth succeeds as alice → SELECT by id=2 → bob's invoice amount returned.

validation.result: dispatch('/api/invoices/2', '', 'Bearer alice-test-token') returned 200 {"id": 2, "owner": "bob", "amount": 200}; unauthenticated request correctly returned 401.

findings.title: Path traversal in /download escapes data/public
findings.evidence: Query parameter name is joined as self.data_root / "public" / name with no canonicalization or containment check before destination.read_text(). Documented contract: downloads serve files under data/public; data/internal is private.
findings.attack_path: Unauthenticated client → GET /download?name=../internal/notes.txt → Path join retains .. segment → read_text() opens data/internal/notes.txt → internal content returned in JSON.

validation.result: dispatch('/download', 'name=../internal/notes.txt', '') returned 200 with content 'Synthetic internal planning note: draft launch date.\n'; resolved path is not relative to data/public.

dismissed_candidates.claim: Baseline CN001/CWE-95 dynamic code evaluation at app.py:22 (eval) is attacker-exploitable
dismissed_candidates.counterevidence: eval("2 + 2") uses a compile-time literal only; no request input reaches eval. Runtime dispatch('/health', '', '') returns {"value": 4} per contract, with no injection surface on this path.

coverage_gaps: Baseline scan only applied rules to app.py; README.md, .cursor/cli.json, and data/* had no baseline rules (heuristic leads only).
No dependency, secret-content, or WSGI server/deployment review; loopback __main__ server path not exercised.
Budget-limited pass: authentication token scheme treated as intentional synthetic test credentials, not assessed as production crypto/session design.
Absence of further baseline matches is not evidence the application is safe; confirmed findings above are independent of unmatched rules.
